title: Publish Terraform module patterns for Private backup bucket + KMS + least-privilege IAM (S3)
creator: Bruno Silva
description:
Context
Private/VPC customers are asking for a supported, copy/pasteable Terraform pattern for backup storage + encryption + least-privilege IAM. Today Solutions/SREs hand-roll bucket/KMS/IAM per account, which is error-prone (common failures: missing kms:Decrypt on restore, overly broad s3:* policies, bucket policy not enforcing SSE-KMS, KMS key policy blocks role usage, lifecycle/retention not set).

Goal
Publish a Redwood-supported Terraform module (and example usage) for AWS that provisions:
1) S3 bucket configured for backup artifacts
2) KMS CMK for envelope encryption / SSE-KMS
3) IAM policies (and optionally roles) for backup writer + restore reader, following least privilege
4) Guardrails: bucket policy enforces TLS + SSE-KMS + denies public access; sane defaults for versioning and lifecycle

Non-goals
- Implementing backup/restore logic (installer CLI owns that; see ENG-9821/ENG-9822)
- Supporting non-AWS backends in this ticket (NFS example tracked separately; GCS is guidance-only for now)
- Multi-region replication as a hard requirement (can be an optional input if easy, otherwise document as follow-up)

Deliverables
A) Module(s) in redwood-terraform repo
- modules/private_backup_s3_kms (name open to bikeshed; prefer explicit “private_backup” naming)
- README with quickstart + security notes
- examples/private-backup-s3-kms (minimal working example)

B) Outputs for installer integration
- bucket_name
- bucket_arn
- kms_key_arn
- kms_key_id
- iam_policy_arn_backup_writer (or json document if we choose data sources)
- iam_policy_arn_restore_reader

C) Docs guidance for customers / Solutions
- “How to wire this into the Private installer values” (env vars / helm values) with a short snippet
- “How to scope IAM to a prefix” guidance (e.g., s3://<bucket>/<customer>/<cluster-id>/)

Proposed module interface (draft)
Required inputs
- name_prefix (string)
- tags (map(string))

Optional inputs (defaults should be safe)
- bucket_name (string, optional; if not set generate)
- backup_prefix (string, default "redwood-private/backups/")
- retention_days (number, default 30)
- enable_versioning (bool, default true)
- kms_key_deletion_window_days (number, default 30)
- create_iam (bool, default true)
- backup_writer_principal_arns (list(string), default [])
- restore_reader_principal_arns (list(string), default [])
- force_destroy (bool, default false)

IAM policy shape (least privilege)
Backup writer should be able to:
- s3:ListBucket (scoped to bucket + prefix condition)
- s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads, s3:ListMultipartUploadParts (scoped to arn:aws:s3:::bucket/prefix*)
- s3:GetObject only if the backup flow needs verification reads (confirm with installer behavior; current backup create does local checksum verification, but may read back metadata)
- kms:Encrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:DescribeKey for the CMK

Restore reader should be able to:
- s3:ListBucket (scoped to prefix)
- s3:GetObject (scoped to prefix*)
- kms:Decrypt, kms:DescribeKey for the CMK

If we generate roles (optional), roles should be assumable by provided principal ARNs with external_id support documented (enterprise requirement). If we don’t generate roles, we still need to generate attachable IAM policies.

Bucket/KMS guardrails
- S3 Block Public Access: enabled
- Bucket policy denies non-TLS (aws:SecureTransport = false)
- Bucket policy denies PutObject without SSE-KMS or with wrong KMS key
- Default encryption: SSE-KMS with our CMK
- Versioning: enabled by default
- Lifecycle:
  - Transition to IA optional (skip for now; keep simple)
  - Expire noncurrent versions after N days (tie to retention_days or fixed sane default)

KMS key policy considerations
We must ensure the key policy allows:
- Account root/admin to manage key
- Backup/restore principals to use key for Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey as appropriate
Important: avoid the common failure mode where IAM policy grants kms:Decrypt but key policy doesn’t allow usage.

Acceptance criteria
- Module passes terraform validate and CI checks in redwood-terraform
- Example applies cleanly in a sandbox AWS account
- Backup writer policy can write an object under the configured prefix; restore reader policy can read/decrypt it
- Bucket policy blocks unencrypted puts and public access
- README clearly states: recommended prefix scoping, how to rotate/replace KMS key, and how to set retention
- Security review sign-off from Marcus Lin or Hanae Suzuki on IAM/KMS policy approach

Testing plan
- Unit-ish: terraform validate + fmt; tflint; checkov/terrascan (whatever is standard in repo)
- Functional: in sandbox account, assume backup role and run aws s3 cp to prefix; verify object has SSE-KMS headers; assume restore role and aws s3 cp back; ensure decrypt works
- Negative: attempt PutObject without SSE headers and confirm AccessDenied

Risks / open questions
- Do we need s3:DeleteObject for restores (cleanup)? Prefer not. Installer should not delete by default.
- Do we need kms:ReEncrypt* (copy/rename)? likely not.
- Prefix scoping: bucket policy can enforce “starts-with” conditions but gets tricky across SDKs; keep policy minimal but include recommended condition patterns.
- Object Lock / WORM retention: some regulated customers will ask; out of scope for first pass.

Implementation notes / links
- Related ticket: ENG-9823 (envelope encryption / KMS provider). This module should align with that KMS usage pattern.
- GitHub PR planned/active: sources/github/redwood-terraform/pr-223-add-s3-kms-backup-module-for-private.json

Updates
2025-02-05 (Bruno)
- Draft module skeleton created with S3 bucket + KMS + two IAM policies.
- Added bucket policy enforcement for aws:SecureTransport and SSE-KMS.
- Open: key policy review with Security; need to confirm principal selection approach.

2025-02-12 (Hanae Suzuki)
- Please ensure key policy allows usage via IAM policies for listed principals; avoid "kms:*" wildcards.
- Add a note on key rotation: enable_rotation = true is fine, but customers still need to retain old key material for decrypting historical backups.

2025-02-18 (Marcus Lin)
- Security review pending: want to see final key policy and whether we ship roles or only policies.
- Prefer shipping policies only (customers attach to existing roles) as default; roles can be optional to avoid surprises with trust policies.

Next steps
- Incorporate Security feedback (policies-only default)
- Add functional test instructions to README
- Request final review from Marcus Lin + Connor O’Brien (release readiness for customers)
- Merge after PM (Vivek) confirms this meets customer handout expectations
